title: Cross-stitch farmyard pig
subtitle: A round pink pig on 14-count Aida in six colours
excerpt: A rotund farmyard pig in profile, stitched in six shades of pink and rose on 14-count white Aida. The design is approximately 65 by 55 stitches and finishes at around 12 by 10 cm. Shading across the body is achieved by blending two strands of adjacent pink shades in the needle.
sourceNotes: Original design. Colour blending (combining two different floss colours in the needle) is documented in DMC technical literature and standard UK cross-stitch method guides.

glossaryTerms.definition: Embroidery thread made from six loosely twisted strands. Cross-stitch uses two or three strands stripped from the skein and recombined in the needle. Different brands (DMC, Anchor) use different numbering systems for their colour ranges.

content.text: Blending two shades in the needle (one strand each of two adjacent colours) gives a soft gradient between tones without the abrupt line of a single-colour fill. This design uses that technique across the pig's belly and haunches to suggest roundness.

items.label: Thread
items.value: DMC 3770 (very light tawny), 3713 (very light salmon), 760 (salmon), 761 (light salmon), 3722 (medium shell pink), 3721 (dark shell pink), 310 (black), 3865 (white)

content.text: For the transition zones between body sections, thread the needle with one strand of the lighter colour and one strand of the darker colour. The resulting stitch sits between the two tones and smooths the gradient.
Begin with the lightest belly tones.
Stitch the centre belly area in 3770 (lightest tone) first, then 3713 moving outward.
Work the body fill outward in graduated tones.
Progress through 760, 761, and 3722 toward the back and haunches. In the transition rows, blend adjacent tones: one strand of 760 and one strand of 761 in the needle.
The inner ear uses 3713; the snout uses 3722 for the outer ring and 760 for the nostril circles.
Add the outline and details in back-stitch.
Outline the pig in 3721 (dark pink) rather than black to keep the look soft. Use 310 only for the eye ring; work a French knot in 3865 for the eye highlight.
Frame in a 15 × 12 cm mount with a white card surround. The pig also works well framed in a 12 cm square hoop with the excess Aida folded neatly behind.
